_readme: The non-English sets Tim has actually ripped on the channel, one entry per
set guide under /sets/.
SEPARATE FROM data/intl-map.json ON PURPOSE. That file answers 'which foreign
set is this English set made from', and it hangs a small panel off an English
guide. This file answers 'which foreign sets did we open packs from', and each
entry becomes a page of its own. A set can appear in both.
ENGLISH NAMES LEAD. Roughly 95% of the audience is in the US, so every page
headlines the English name and keeps the native script as a subtitle. The
native name is still the verifiable one, so it is always shown, never dropped.
HOW EACH ENTRY WAS CHECKED, against api.tcgdex.net on 2026-08-12:
- the set id resolves in that language and the native name matches
- Korean and Chinese sets share their id with the Japanese set they are
translated from, so ko/SV6 was checked against ja/SV6 (both 101 cards)
- the English equivalent was checked on release order and card counts
THE CHECK THAT DOES NOT TRANSFER. For Japanese sets, 'the Japanese set comes
out first' is a good test, because Japan is where sets originate. It is WRONG
for Korean and Chinese: ko/SV6 shipped 2024-06-21, a month AFTER English
Twilight Masquerade. They are not late English sets, they are translations of
the Japanese set on their own regional schedule. Never 'fix' a Korean entry
because its date looks late.
WHAT TCGDEX ACTUALLY HAS, measured, not assumed:
- no set logos or symbols for ANY of these, in any language
- card lists for the 7 sets flagged hasCards below, images for only 2
- Korean and Chinese sets carry a cardCount but ZERO card records, so their
counts cannot be verified. Those entries use dataFrom to read the checklist
from the Japanese set instead, and the page says where it came from.
DO NOT add an entry from a card-site article. Check it against the API.

`published` is the date a guide first appeared and MUST NOT be edited. It feeds datePublished in the page's structured data; before it existed both datePublished and dateModified were set to the sync date, so all 13 guides told Google they were published today, every day, and dateModified carried no information at all.
source: TCGdex (api.tcgdex.net/v2), card names via PokeAPI dex numbers

ja-abyss-eye.note: Released 2026-05-22, about two months ahead of the English Pitch Black. Same set, same chase lineup, Japanese print run.

ja-ninja-spinner.note: 120 cards against Chaos Rising's 122, out roughly ten weeks earlier.

ja-nihil-zero.nameNote: The set itself is certain: the code, the card count and the release date all check out. The English name is less settled. The card database we read transcribes the Japanese name in a way that does not come out as Nihil Zero, but Nihil Zero is what is on the packs we opened and what everyone calls it. We went with the packs.

ja-mega-symphonia.note: Half of English Mega Evolution. Japan split it into two 92 card sets released the same day, which English merged into one 188 card set.

ja-mega-brave.note: The other half of English Mega Evolution, out the same day as Mega Symphonia.

ja-stellar-miracle.note: The Japanese set behind Stellar Crown, out about eight weeks earlier.

ja-cyber-judge.siblingName: Wild Force (ワイルドフォース, SV5K)
ja-cyber-judge.note: English Temporal Forces is built from two Japanese sets released together: Cyber Judge and Wild Force, 71 cards each.

ja-violet-ex.siblingName: Scarlet ex (スカーレットex, SV1S)
ja-violet-ex.note: The set that opened the Scarlet and Violet era in Japan. Violet ex and Scarlet ex together became the English Scarlet & Violet base set.

ko-clay-burst.note: The Korean printing of the Japanese Clay Burst. Clay Burst and Snow Hazard together became English Paldea Evolved. This is the set with the Iono chase card.

ko-crimson-haze.note: A smaller Japanese subset whose cards were spread across more than one English set rather than becoming one of its own, so the English match is partial rather than one to one.

ko-mask-of-change.note: The Korean printing of the set behind English Twilight Masquerade. Korea got it 2024-06-21, a month after the English release, which is normal: it follows the Japanese schedule, not the English one.

ko-battle-partners.dataNote: TCGdex has no Korean record for this set at all, so everything on this page comes from the Japanese printing it was translated from.
ko-battle-partners.note: The set behind English Journey Together. Its chase is Lillie's Clefairy ex, #184. Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex belongs to Destined Rivals, not this set.

zh-gem-pack-2.note: A genuine Chinese exclusive. There is no Japanese or English counterpart: the id returns nothing in every other language. Gem Pack is a small 15 card Chinese series that reprints fan favourite lines, and Vol. 2 is the Eevee one.
